authority: ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 sections 20.4.44 and 20.4.74 place an object-data bit-size boundary before the bodies and handle tails of R13/R14 DICTIONARY and DICTIONARYVAR records.
source: Adapted the guard from locally available diverged tracked-branch commit 9a2f6af1bc7d84d7b3c85ee1ae32ea6a30f3188f; expanded the generated DICTIONARYVAR control to cover R14. The branch was not merged or overwritten.
finding: The legacy object-data completion check treated a zero body boundary as a fallback, allowing a DICTIONARY or DICTIONARYVAR body to be published without proving separation from its following handle stream.
change: Require a nonzero, exactly consumed inline body boundary for R13/R14 DICTIONARY and DICTIONARYVAR bodies; keep other versions' completion behavior unchanged.
validation: The new R13 zero-boundary DICTIONARY control failed before the fix. Afterward, the generated R13 dictionary and R13/R14 DICTIONARYVAR zero-boundary refusal/reset/corrected-retry controls pass, as do the owning dictionary CTest and DWG object-vector executable in normal and AddressSanitizer builds.

Both earlier specification-directed AC1012 physical dictionary frames pass the source-frame parser/refusal/retry selector. The current converter reads all 199 reported frames in each root-case-aligned ODA-generated AC1012 source with zero parser failures, then preserves an existing destination on the native-merge qualification refusal; one custom class and one unsupported object are skipped per source.
limits: The source controls and raw frame census do not establish native AutoCAD merge behavior or complete semantic support.
Selected code and test inputs changed, so earlier qualification digests and hosted results do not qualify this candidate.
